title: A protocol to evaluate epithelial regeneration after inducing cell loss in zebrafish larvae
protocol: Prepare zebrafish larvae at day 4 post-fertilization for metronidazole treatment.
Pipette 15–20 larvae into each well of a 12-well tissue culture plate.
Formulate treatment groups with no NTR-mCherry and Metronidazole.
Create another treatment group with no NTR-mCherry and no Metronidazole.
Prepare a third treatment group with NTR-mCherry and Metronidazole.
Establish a fourth treatment group with NTR-mCherry and no Metronidazole.
Remove as much media as possible and replace with 2 mL of E3 media.
Add 20 μL of 1 M metronidazole for a final concentration of 10 μM.
Place all samples at 28.5°C for 5 h.
Prepare additional treatment groups to include chemical compounds to be screened and their corresponding controls.
Remove E3-MTZ and replace it with 2 mL fresh E3 with no MTZ.
Replace E3 with fresh E3 two more times with no incubation.
Proceed to either determining the amount of extrusion-induced tissue area loss in the tail fin epithelium or detection and visualization of cell loss-induced proliferation sections of the protocol.
Measure the total area of the tail fin in treated larvae.
Determine the extent of cell loss and tissue area reduction between different treatment groups.
Compare the overall extent of tissue area loss (or protection from cell loss and epithelial damage) between a control and experimental group.

Fix larvae for the early damage assay by placing them in a 1.7 mL Eppendorf tube containing 1 mL of 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) in phosphate buffered saline (PBS) solution containing 0.05% Triton X-100.
Rock the tube on a three-dimensional gentle mixer overnight at 4°C.
Remove the PFA solution and rinse samples twice with 750 μL PBS-Triton X-100 (0.1%) without incubation.
Wash samples with 750 μL PBS-Triton X-100 (0.5%) and rock on mixer for 5 min at room temperature.
Repeat the wash step two additional times.
Prepare a DAPI solution by adding DAPI to PBS-Triton X-100 (0.5%) at 1:1000.
Add 750 μL of PBS-Triton X-100 with 1:1000 DAPI to samples and rock on mixer for 30 min at room temperature.
Wash samples three times with PBS-Triton X-100 (0.5%) and rock on mixer for five minutes each at room temperature.
Wash samples one time with 750 μL PBS-Triton X-100 (0.1%) and rock on mixer for 5 min at room temperature.
Rinse samples with PBS and mix by inverting tube by hand two to three times.
Mount larvae on microscope slides and seal with clear nail polish.
Obtain images of the zebrafish caudal fin.
Use the polygon tool in Fiji to first draw a vertical line that runs from the dorsal edge of the tail to the ventral edge of the fin.
Complete the polygon by tracing the distal edge of the caudal fin from the basal end of the notochord until reaching the dorsal edge where the line was started.
Use the measuring tool in Fiji to calculate the area included in the polygon.
Divide resulting data into categories based on area thresholds.
Capture both dorsal and ventral edges of the tail fin in imaging.
Use a 10× image for quantification.
Apply digital zoom (0.6×) to improve measurement accuracy.
Standardize methodology for larger fin regions when applicable.
Fix larvae according to the modified fixation protocol.
Prepare custom in situ probes from Molecular Instruments.
Detect changes in mRNA using hybridization chain reaction (HCR).
Fix larvae after 5 h MTZ exposure by placing them in a 1.7 mL Eppendorf tube containing 1 mL of 4% paraformaldehyde in PBS solution with 0.1% Triton X-100.
Rock the Eppendorf tube on a nutator overnight at 4°C.
Wash larvae twice for 5 min each with 750 μL PBS.
Wash larvae twice for 5 min each with 750 μL PBS containing 0.1% Tween-20 (PBS-Tween).
Postfix larvae for 20 min with freshly made 4% paraformaldehyde solution and rock at room temperature.
Briefly wash larvae twice with 750 μL PBS-Tween.
Wash larvae twice for 5 min each with 750 μL PBS-Tween.
Transfer 10–12 larvae into a new Eppendorf tube.
Mount samples as flat as possible for imaging on MatTek dishes using low melt agarose.
Image samples using a Zeiss LSM-800 confocal microscope at both 10× and 20× magnifications.
Wash each well three times with 2 mL of E3 media.
Replace all epithelial restoration compounds for compensatory proliferation portion of the experiment at 28.5°C overnight.
Prepare a fresh 10 mM BrdU + 5% DMSO solution in E3.
Replace E3 in recovery wells with 2 mL BrdU solution and place at 28.5°C for 30 minutes.
Wash each well twice with 2 mL of E3 and place at 28.5°C for 30 minutes.
Fix larvae for the early damage assay by placing them in 1 mL of 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) containing 0.05% Triton X-100 in PBS and rock on a nutator overnight at 4°C.
After overnight fixation, remove PFA solution.
Wash samples three times with 750 μL PBS-Triton X-100 (0.5%) and rock on mixer for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Wash samples three times with ddH2O and rock on mixer for 10 minutes.
Replace ddH2O with 2 N HCl solution in ddH2O containing 0.5% Triton-X100, incubate at room temperature on a nutator for 45 minutes.
Wash samples three times with 750 μL PBS-Triton X-100 (0.5%).
Block samples for 1 hour with 1 mL freshly made Block Solution at room temperature on a nutator.
Dilute primary (Rat-anti BrdU) antibody (1:200) in freshly made Block Solution.
Incubate samples in primary antibody overnight on gentle rocking mixer at 4°C.
Rinse samples three times with 750 μL PBS-Triton X-100 (0.5%) and mix by inverting the tube by hand two to three times.
Wash samples three times with 750 μL PBS-Triton X-100 (0.5%).
Rock samples on a mixer for 20 min each at room temperature.
Block samples for 1 h with 1 mL freshly made Block Solution at room temperature on a nutator.
Dilute secondary (Goat-anti Rat) antibody (1:200) in freshly made Block Solution.
Incubate samples in the diluted secondary antibody overnight on a nutator at 4°C, keeping samples covered or in dark.
Rinse samples three times with 750 μL PBS-Triton X-100 (0.5%) and mix by inverting the tube by hand two to three times.
Wash samples three times with 750 μL PBS-Triton X-100 (0.5%) and rock on a mixer for 5 min at room temperature.
Prepare a DAPI solution by adding DAPI to PBS-Triton X-100 (0.5%) at 1:1000.
Add 750 μL of PBS-Triton X-100 (0.5%) with 1:1000 DAPI to samples and rock on a mixer for 30 min at room temperature.
Rinse samples three times with 750 μL PBS-Triton X-100 (0.5%) and mix by inverting the tube by hand two to three times.
Wash samples one time with 750 μL PBS-Triton X-100 (0.1%) and rock on a mixer for 5 min at room temperature.
Rinse samples with PBS and mix by inverting the tube by hand two to three times.
Mount samples for imaging.
Use EdU, CldU or IdU as an alternative to BrdU in studies requiring multiple rounds of labeling dividing cells.
Administer BrdU at the 18 hour recovery time point to label dividing cells.
Allow larvae to recover and treat with a different nucleotide analog such as CldU or IdU after 24 hours.
Detect CldU or IdU along with BrdU to distinguish cells that divided at one of the two time points (BrdU positive or CldU/IdU positive).
Detect cells that divided during both time points by being both BrdU and CldU/IdU positive.
Use antibodies to detect phosphorylation states of key proteins such as Histone H3 for cell division determination.
Note: This approach labels fewer cells compared to nucleotide analogs incorporated during S phase, like BrdU.
